decision: Close the H100 W4 optimization line without another endpoint or c96 component arm. Actual FP8 KV update plus supported local/global paged attention is material but far too small to explain or repair the 66.63% complete-request miss, and scheduler/context plus CUDA launch overhead is negligible.

measured_h100_c128.runtime: vLLM 0.19.1.dev6+g6d4a8e6d2; NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3; SM90; CUDA 12.9

source_backed_causal_trace.prior_global_zero_fixture: The prior fixture passed per_layer_sliding_window=-1. TritonAttentionImpl treats any non-None integer as (sliding_window-1, 0), producing (-2, 0); the unified kernel then receives a truthy negative sliding-window sentinel and masks the V path. This was a fixture defect, not unsupported global attention.
source_backed_causal_trace.supported_global_route: Passing None produces the installed implementation window (-1, -1). At c128, 128 sequences also exceed the global 2-D threshold 128/4=32. The actual unified FP8 producer and selected consumer then returned finite nonzero output with abs_max 0.51171875 and mean 0.4979850649833679.
source_backed_causal_trace.endpoint_scheduler_policy: The measured endpoint used max_num_batched_tokens=8192 and max_num_seqs=128. A 4214-token prompt leaves capacity for approximately one full prompt prefill alongside decode tokens, creating a TTFT/queue staircase; this is scheduling policy waiting, not measured Python scheduler or CUDA launch cost.

endpoint_reconciliation.interpretation: Queue policy is visible and material, but even the earliest c128 completion exceeds the entire target batch ceiling. Deleting all measured KV update and attention work still leaves a 2.748x miss. No measured or tightly bounded attention, KV, scheduler-CPU, or launch change qualifies for promotion, and no endpoint retry is justified.

evidence_boundary: Checkpoint-free component mechanism evidence only. No checkpoint, endpoint retry, c96 component transfer, quality, deployability, or production eligibility claim.
